title: On the Robustness of Propagating Bound States in the Continuum
summary: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are localized eigenmodes with their frequencies in the radiation continuum of scattering states. The existence of a BIC implies the loss of uniqueness for scattering problems with given incident waves. Perturbed wave systems close to the ideal ones with a BIC exhibit strong resonance effects that are essential to numerous practical applications. A question of fundamental importance is whether a BIC is robust, i.e., whether it can continue its existence when the structure is slightly perturbed.
